subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should operator-managed internal hooks receive outbound content before typed security policy, after policy succeeds, or should pre-delivery content remain available only to typed plugin hooks?
rationale: The repository currently documents internal hooks as coarse side effects and typed hooks as the policy surface; exposing outbound content adds a security-sensitive lifecycle contract whose timing cannot be selected mechanically.

options.title: Add a post-policy observer
options.body: Approve a canonical observation-only `message:sending` event that receives final non-cancelled content after the typed policy hook and is documented as unable to rewrite or cancel.

options.title: Keep typed hooks exclusive
options.body: Do not add the internal event and direct guardrail or cancellation users to a plugin using the existing typed `message_sending` API.

options.title: Expose pre-policy content
options.body: Intentionally expose original content before policy, with explicit documentation that cancelled or rewritten content is observable by internal hooks.

recommendation.title: Add a post-policy observer
recommendation.body: Approve a canonical observation-only `message:sending` event that receives final non-cancelled content after the typed policy hook and is documented as unable to rewrite or cancel.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related maintainer-associated work already defines the exactly-once outbound policy boundary across channel delivery paths.
